title: Scripts: commands you saved
summary: Anything you type twice can become a file you run with one line. Same steps, same result, every time, and Claude can write it for you. Builds on: pipes (A6).
note: Names, companies and files here are **made-up examples**.

props.title: ~/Documents/Sales/monday-report.sh
props.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Monday report: Acme orders, by region
cd ~/Documents/Sales
grep "Acme" orders.csv > acme.csv
wc -l acme.csv
cut -d, -f3 acme.csv | sort | uniq -c
cp acme.csv ~/Desktop/acme-weekly.csv

props.title: Write the steps down once
props.body: A script is a recipe card for the computer: the same steps, in the same order, kept in a file.

props.title: ~/Documents/Sales/justfile
props.code:
# Acme orders, by region
report:
    bash monday-report.sh
# Delete the working copy
clean:
    rm -f acme.csv
# Copy orders.csv into Backups
backup:
    mkdir -p ~/Backups
    cp orders.csv ~/Backups/

props.text: Make the Monday report stop with a clear message if orders.csv is missing.
I added a check near the top of **monday-report.sh**: without orders.csv it now stops and says so. With it, the report runs as before.

props.title: Have Claude write one
props.ask: Write a script that lists every CSV in this folder with its line count, then show me what it does before running it.
props.expect: Claude writes a short script and explains it line by line. Read it, then let it run: it gives the same list every time, until the folder changes.

steps.title: Every Monday, by hand
steps.text: Every Monday you type the same five commands to pull this week's Acme orders out of the sales export. (`>` saves what a command prints into a file.) Five lines to remember, and to get right, every week.

steps.title: Write them down once
steps.text: A **script** is a file of commands you can run with one line. These are the same five commands, saved as `monday-report.sh`. The first line says which shell runs it (bash, which also comes with every Mac); lines starting with `#` are notes for people.

steps.title: Run it with one line
steps.text: Now Monday is one line: `bash monday-report.sh`. It runs every command in the file, in order. (Run `chmod +x monday-report.sh` once and `./monday-report.sh` works too: `chmod +x` marks a file as runnable.)

steps.title: Same result, every time
steps.text: Run it next week, or ten times today: it does exactly the same thing. That's **deterministic** again (same input, same result, every time), and it's why a script beats remembering.

recipe.title: Same steps, same result
recipe.body: Follow the card and you get the same dish every time. A script is **deterministic**: same input, same result, every time.

steps.title: It doesn't notice what changed
steps.text: This week the export arrived as `orders-october.csv`. A cook would notice the missing flour; the script just carries on. `grep` complains, and an empty report lands on your Desktop. Read a script before you run it.

recipe.title: It follows the card, even when things changed
recipe.body: A cook would notice the flour is missing. A script does exactly what it says, even when the situation is different.

lines.text: (this week the file is called orders-october.csv)
grep: orders.csv: No such file or directory
(an empty acme-weekly.csv is now on your Desktop)

steps.title: A menu of recipes
steps.text: A **justfile** collects a folder's scripts and commands into a menu. `just --list` shows the menu; `just report` runs one recipe. `just` isn't built into macOS: install it once, with Homebrew (`brew install just`).

recipe.title: A box of recipe cards
recipe.body: Each recipe has a name and a one-line note. `just --list` reads you the menu; you pick one by name.

lines.text:
Available recipes:
    backup # Copy orders.csv into Backups
    clean  # Delete the working copy
    report # Acme orders, by region
(it runs bash monday-report.sh: the same report as before)

steps.title: Claude writes, you keep the script
steps.text: You don't have to write scripts yourself. Ask Claude Code to write or fix one, then read what it changed. Claude does the writing (probabilistic); the saved script then runs the same way every time (deterministic).

script.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Monday report: Acme orders, by region
cd ~/Documents/Sales
if [ ! -f orders.csv ]; then
    echo "Stopped: orders.csv is missing"
    exit 1
fi
grep "Acme" orders.csv > acme.csv
wc -l acme.csv
cut -d, -f3 acme.csv | sort | uniq -c
cp acme.csv ~/Desktop/acme-weekly.csv

steps.title: The whole picture
steps.text: Type it twice, save it once. Scripts and a justfile hold the steps that must be the same every time; Claude helps write them and judges what's new. Your part: read before you run.
